label.purpose: Nav tabs, table headers, stat labels — short and structural.

shadows.name: bevel-highlight
shadows.purpose: Top-edge light catch on every metal surface at rest.

shadows.name: bevel-shadow
shadows.purpose: Paired dark bottom edge, at rest.

shadows.name: press-shadow
shadows.purpose: Replaces bevel-highlight on :active, sells physical sink-in.

motion.name: shimmer-sweep
motion.purpose: One-time diagonal light sweep across a metal surface on hover.

motion.name: press-spring
motion.purpose: Physical sink-in on :active, springs back on release.

components.name: Chrome Button (Blue)
components.description: Primary action button: blue-to-navy chrome gradient with a diagonal shimmer sweep on hover and a physical press.
components.css: .ds-btn-chrome-blue { position: relative; overflow: hidden; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 11px 22px; border-radius: 10px; border: 2px solid transparent; font-family: 'Exo 2', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; background-image: linear-gradient(180deg, #5b86ff 0%, #2a55dc 42%, #1a2f8f 78%, #291f6b 100%), linear-gradient(135deg, #f2f5fb 0%, #bdccff 14%, #5b76d6 30%, #24306e 45%, #7fa8ff 58%, #9a7fff 66%, #24306e 78%, #c3cad6 92%, #f2f5fb 100%); background-clip: padding-box, border-box; background-origin: padding-box, border-box; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.3), inset 0 -6px 12px -6px rgba(0,10,50,0.6), 0 0 26px rgba(70,120,255,0.5); transition: transform 0.05s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-chrome-blue:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.97); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 6px rgba(0,10,40,0.8); }

components.name: Nav Tab
components.description: One tab in the site-wide gunmetal navigation strip: icon + label, shimmer on hover, glowing ring when active.
components.css: .ds-nav-tab { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; padding: 10px 14px; font-family: 'Exo 2', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.4px; color: #aab6d6; text-decoration: none; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(140,170,255,0.14) 0%, rgba(140,170,255,0) 14%, rgba(0,0,10,0) 76%, rgba(0,0,20,0.3) 100%); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(180,205,255,0.14), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-nav-tab--active { color: #fff; background-color: rgba(4,8,20,0.5); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.7), inset 0 0 10px rgba(59,130,246,0.3); }

components.name: Game Card
components.description: Square game tile: gunmetal-blue frame, radial glow anchored bottom, cursor-follow light + shimmer on hover.
components.css: .ds-game-card { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; aspect-ratio: 1/1; border-radius: 10px; border: 2px solid transparent; text-decoration: none; overflow: hidden; background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 120%, rgba(60,130,255,0.1), transparent 60%), linear-gradient(180deg, #202840 0%, #12172a 45%, #080a14 100%) padding-box, linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(190,215,255,0.5) 0%, rgba(130,160,255,0.2) 16%, rgba(40,50,80,0.32) 55%, rgba(130,160,255,0.28) 100%) border-box; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(190,210,255,0.14), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5); transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease, transform 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-game-card:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(200,220,255,0.24), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.4), inset 0 0 16px rgba(90,150,255,0.2), 0 8px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.45), 0 0 20px rgba(59,130,246,0.32); } .ds-game-card:active { transform: scale(0.97); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.65), inset 0 0 12px rgba(59,130,246,0.3); } .ds-game-card-number { font-family: 'Orbitron', sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 16px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #ffffff 0%, #d3ddf0 45%, #9fb0d0 100%); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent; }

narrative.overview: Quest Zone reads as the command bridge of a starship, not a website chrome-plated for effect: a real universe fills the void behind everything (a canvas starfield with twinkling stars, drifting nebula wisps, and rare distant galaxies, its exact composition re-rolled every page load), and every interactive surface — nav bar, buttons, game tiles, panels — is machined from the same brushed-titanium/gunmetal material, lit from a cold blue seam rather than a warm studio light. The bridge metaphor is literal at the component level: the nav bar is built from angular, riveted plates with cyan seam-lighting between segments, exactly like a physical control console, not a flat CSS bar wearing a gradient. The system is deliberately restrained given how much surface area it covers: the metallic material family is the one recurring texture used everywhere rather than a different treatment per section, so fifteen-plus pages spanning the homepage, Highscores, the full Profile suite, and the Admin Zone all read as one machine. Motion is a small, repeated vocabulary — a diagonal shimmer sweep on hover, a physical sink-in-and-spring-back on click, a soft cursor-follow glow — reused verbatim on every interactive element rather than invented fresh per component.
keyCharacteristics: A live, randomized deep-space canvas background behind every page, never a static image
One shared brushed-gunmetal + blue-seam-light material used for the nav bar, every button variant, and every game/content tile
A diagonal shimmer sweep + tactile press-and-spring physical feedback on every clickable metal surface
Orbitron for anything that announces itself; Exo 2 for anything read in a sentence
Status/semantic color (green, red, gold) is reserved and never used for ordinary chrome

rules.name: The Cold-Light Rule
rules.body: Every light source in this system — glow, highlight, seam, shimmer — is blue-white, never warm.

rules.name: The Reserved-Status-Color Rule
rules.body: Green and gold never appear on ordinary chrome, only on the specific status or reward they signal.

rules.name: The One-Voice-Per-Job Rule
rules.body: Orbitron announces; Exo 2 explains. A control never mixes the two faces in the same string.

rules.name: The Rest-Is-Quiet Rule
rules.body: No component glows or casts an outer shadow at rest — only the beveled inset pair. Glow is a response to state, never ambient decoration.

dos: Do build every new interactive surface from the same metal-bevel + shimmer + press vocabulary already used by the nav, buttons, and game tiles.
Do keep the starfield canvas as the one full-bleed background element on every page.
Do reserve outer glow/shadow for state changes.
Do use Orbitron for anything structural or numeric and Exo 2 for anything read in a sentence.
donts: Don't introduce a warm accent color anywhere in the chrome.
Don't use a flat, un-beveled, drop-shadow-only card style anywhere meant to feel premium.
Don't add a hover effect that isn't already in the vocabulary.
Don't put game-genre-category tabs or any other nav content that isn't a real, working destination into the primary nav.
